thread.title: Outside the Box: These 2 shocks will jolt stocks higher — and 15 smart ways to prepare for that move

author: Stocks News Feed
title: Outside the Box: These 2 shocks will jolt stocks higher — and 15 smart ways to prepare for that move
text:
Investor sentiment has now fallen prey to the stock -market equivalent of cardiac arrest.
That’s understandable. Popular stocks like Amazon.com
 AMZN, +1.93%
 Apple
 AAPL, +0.88%
 and Facebook
 FB, -1.61%
 are all in bear-market territory. So are broad sector indexes like the Vanguard Energy exchange-traded fund
 VDE, -0.41%
 the SPDR S&P Biotech ETF
 XBI, +0.72%
 and SPDR S&P Homebuilders ETF
 XHB, -0.83%
Sentiment is now so dead that it suggests the next leg of the stock market is up, in the contrarian sense.
Consider the ratio of open interest in puts (a negative bet) to calls (a more hopeful position). This ratio has spiked to levels frequently followed by rallies, says Doug Ramsey, chief investment officer of The Leuthold Group. “That would support my call for a possible bounce into year-end,” he says.
Insiders, the people with the front-row seats on business confirm they expect the next major move is up. Insiders are bullish overall with purchases outweighing sales — an unusual tilt for them. They usually sell more stock than they buy.
In analysis I do of insider activity for my stock newsletter Brush Up on Stocks , I’ve noticed that insiders are now particularly bullish in cyclical sectors like auto parts, home building and related retailers, real estate, chemicals and energy. This makes sense. Cyclical stocks are among those that have been hit the hardest. So they’re likely to rebound the most in a market reversal.
Of course for markets to firm up again, something is going to have to jolt investor sentiment out of cardiac arrest and bring it back to life. Here are the two chest paddles that will soon provide the shocks that investor sentiment needs.
Right chest paddle: The Fed backs off Throughout this recovery since 2009 every time the Federal Reserve has started to pull away the comforter of low interest rates, investors have thrown a temper tantrum until the Fed backs off. That’s what investors are doing now, and expect the standard Fed response to soon happen again.
This isn’t just about soothing spoiled stock investors. There are good reasons to be worried about the aggressive Fed rate hike path given many clear signs of a slowdown in the U.S. and throughout the world. Global purchasing managers indexes are rolling over. Leading economic indicators like home prices , automobile sales, oil prices and commodity prices are weakening.
“We’re seeing swiftest deterioration in the global economic data in three years,” says Larry McDonald of The Bear Traps Report . “The trends in the U.S., Europe, Japan, and China are all pointing towards an upcoming global recession.”
Bond markets confirm trouble ahead. The spread between yields on high-yield bonds and 10-year U.S. Treasurys
 TMUBMUSD10Y, +0.36%
 is widening.
Read: Trump again lashes out at Powell, says he’s ‘not even a little bit happy’ about naming him Fed chief
The upshot in all of this: “The U.S. equity market will crash in 1987 style if the Fed plays tough guy. It’s that simple,” says McDonald. He thinks U.S. stocks could fall another 40% in this scenario. This risk will make the Fed back away from its proposed course of aggressive rate hikes in 2019.
“The Fed will have no choice but to pause on their policy path if they want to delay the end of the current economic expansion,” says McDonald. Central banks around the world will follow suit. We just saw signs of this in dovish comments from European Central Bank President Mario Draghi. “We see these comments as just the beginning of a wave of central bank talk that will shift dovish and move markets,” says McDonald.
Read: Fed flags concerns over corporate debt in first-ever financial stability report
The counter argument here is that it’s not the Fed’s job to manage the stock market. But this view is off target. At some point, the dramatic wealth destruction of a sharp market decline darkens outlooks so much that it reduces investment, which hurts growth. Investor fear also raises borrowing costs as it drives up bond yields. So calming investor fear to keep the expansion going is logically part of the Fed’s job. Besides, the stock market is one of the best leading economic indicators, so the big pullback is a negative signal on growth. Fix worries about growth, and stocks recover.
Don’t be mislead by strong third-quarter growth. That’s history and the markets are forward-looking. Besides, it was an anomaly based on one-offs like inventory building ahead of trade tariffs as well as the impact of tax cuts and fiscal stimulus.
Read: Economy grew 3.5% in third quarter, pushes corporate profits to 6-year high, GDP shows
Left chest paddle: The U.S. and China kiss and make up The economies of both China and the U.S. are now suffering due to the war on trade. This puts pressure on both President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to do something about it, and they will. “They’re staring down the barrel of an ugly global recession. President Trump and Xi know they must do a deal,” says McDonald.
Yes, Trump just reiterated a desire to impose tariffs on Chinese goods. But McDonald views this as “hardball” ahead of the Group of 20 (G-20) summit this week in Argentina, where Trump and Xi will meet. Signs of progress here could boost U.S. stocks .
Read: Here are 4 routes to defuse U.S.-China tensions
How to position for the next leg up in stocks Insiders heavily favor cyclical names right now, and that’s one way to go. There’s recently been significant insider buying in homebuilding-related stocks like Meritage Homes
 MTH, -1.45%
 Home Depot
 HD, -0.24%
 and Lowe’s Cos
 LOW, +0.52%
 Insiders also favor cyclical names in energy, chemicals and the auto sector like Murphy Oil
 MUR, +1.74%
 Platform Specialty Products
 PAH, -0.45%
 and American Axle & Manufacturing
 AXL, +1.10%
While the S&P 500
 SPX, +0.43%
 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average
 DJIA, +0.79%
 will do well in any rebound ahead, McDonald likes Horizons DAX Germany
 DAX, -0.16%
 and iShares MSCI Europe Financials
 EUFN, -0.27%
 as plays on a rebound in European stocks , and XHB, SPDR S&P Oil & Gas Exploration & Production
 XOP, -0.63%
 and United States Oil Fund
 USO, -1.56%
 as cyclical plays in a rebound.
He likes iShares China Large-Cap
 FXI, +0.64%
 and KraneShares CSI China Internet
 KWEB, -0.02%
 as plays on China stocks that will benefit, and iShares MSCI Emerging Markets
 EEM, +0.32%
 SPDR S&P Metals and Mining
 XME, +0.50%
 and VanEck Vectors Gold Miners
 GDX, -0.05%
 as plays on expected dollar weakness as the Fed backs away from its aggressive policy stance.
At the time of publication, Michael Brush had no positions in any stocks mentioned in this column. Brush has suggested AMZN, FB, HD and LOW, in his stock newsletter Brush Up on Stocks . Brush is a Manhattan-based financial writer who has covered business for the New York Times and The Economist Group, and he attended Columbia Business School in the Knight-Bagehot program.
